concepts.label: Absolute Place
concepts.description: An absolute place is defined without reference to other places.

concepts.label: Abstract Entity
concepts.description: An abstract concept is a concept which does not (necessarily) have a referent in either the physical or the mental world. Abstract entities are (proto)mathematical, formal entities, entities which have a purely formal, logical or mathematical meaning. As all concepts are abstractions, one may arg...

concepts.label: Act of Law
concepts.description: Act of law: a public act by a legislative body which creates an expression with legal status; the legal status depends on the jurisdiction of the legislative body.

concepts.label: Action
concepts.description: An action is a change which is brought about by a single agent, playing a role. The agent is the holder of some indended outcome of the action: an action is always intentional. The intention of the agent has usually corresponds with an expectation the intended outcome to be brought about: the age...

concepts.label: Action Power
concepts.description: An action-power consists in a generic power to produce a legal effect through an action determining it. Also called Subjections

concepts.label: Agent
concepts.description: An agent is any owl:Thing which can act, i.e. play the 'actor' role wrt. an action

concepts.label: Allowed
concepts.description: See normatively qualified. Alternative labels: permitted, sanctioned, let, licensed.

concepts.label: Allowed And Disallowed
concepts.description: Something which is both allowed and disallowed through some norm

concepts.label: Annulment
concepts.description: Class

concepts.label: Application
concepts.description: When a local act applies in the local legal system normative supra-ordered such as when a region applies an EU directive or a decree it applies the normative contant in some act

concepts.label: Application Date
concepts.description: The date when a modification is applied to the destination legislative document. The date can be instantaneous, in the future or in the past. Normally this date coincides with the date of efficacy of the text in which the modification takes place.

concepts.label: Application Interval
concepts.description: This is the interval during which a normative document, or fragment, produces the consequences that the normative provision establishes.

concepts.label: Argument
concepts.description: An argument is a reason that is expressed through some medium

concepts.label: Artifact
concepts.description: A physical object created by some person to fulfill a particular purpose

concepts.label: Assertion
concepts.description: The assertion is subject to a fit between words and world, in Searle's terms. It's propositional content can be true of false. If it is inconsistent with other assertions, beliefs, observations, it may come to be considered false.

concepts.label: Assignment
concepts.description: A public act that attributes a power to perform a public act to a public body.

concepts.label: Association
concepts.description: A voluntary association (also sometimes called an unincorporated association, or just an association) is a group of individuals who voluntarily enter into an agreement to form a body (or organization) to accomplish a purpose.

concepts.label: Assumption
concepts.description: proposes something that usually is the case, although there is no specific evidence that it is true in this particular case

concepts.label: Atom
concepts.description: An atom is the most basic (undivisible) part of an LKIF rule (cf. Deliverable 1.1)

concepts.label: Belief
concepts.description: Someting an agent 'believes in', i.e. holds as true

concepts.label: Belief In Violation
concepts.description: A belief in some violation

concepts.label: Cause
concepts.description: A cause is an epistemic role played by something which is the outcome of a (chain) of processes

concepts.label: Change
concepts.description: A change is a difference between the situation before and after the change occurs (the event of the change). A change can be instantaneous

concepts.label: Co-operative
concepts.description: An autonomous association of persons united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social, and cultural needs and aspirations through a jointly-owned and democratically-controlled enterprise.

concepts.label: Code
concepts.description: A legal code bears one or more norms, all of which are uttered by some legislative body. It cannot bear expressions which are not uttered by a legislative body.

concepts.label: Code of Conduct
concepts.description: a code outlining the responsibilities of or best practice for an individual or organisation, such as a set of principles of good corporate behaviour adopted by a business\

concepts.label: Collaborative Plan
concepts.description: A collaborative plan is a plan which is shared (and executed) between at least two agents a and b.

concepts.label: Communicated Attitude
concepts.description: A communictated attitude is a propositional attitude involved in an act of communication.

concepts.label: Company
concepts.description: A company refers to a legal entity formed which has a separate legal identity from its members, and is ordinarily incorporated to undertake commercial business. Although some jurisdictions refer to unincorporated entities as companies, in most jurisdictions the term refers only to incorporated en...

concepts.label: Composition
concepts.description: A composition has multiple parts, the components should meet

concepts.label: Comprehensive Place
concepts.description: A place is comprehensive if it always covers every place (and thus also every location-complex) and every object.

concepts.label: Continuation
concepts.description: The continuation of a change, once initiated

concepts.label: Contract
concepts.description: A contract bears one or more norms, all of which are uttered by some natural person or legal person. It cannot bear expressions which are uttered by a different kind of agent.

concepts.label: Corporation
concepts.description: A corporation is a legal entity which, while being composed of natural persons, exists completely separately from them. This separation gives the corporation unique powers which other legal entities lack.

concepts.label: Creation
concepts.description: An act which results in the creation of some entity/individual

concepts.label: Custom
concepts.description: The collective memory of some group of agents, i.e. propositions beared by custom are shared (i.e. held) by all members of the group

concepts.label: Customary Law
concepts.description: In law, custom, or customary law consists of established patterns of behaviour that can be objectively verified within a particular social setting.

concepts.label: Decision
concepts.description: NOTE: Cannot express that the 'promised' act corresponds to the act qualified by the statement in writing

concepts.label: Declaration
concepts.description: Searle: the successful performance of a declaration is sufficient to bring about the fit between words and world, to make the propositional content true. In other words, if there is an inconsistency between the declaration and assertions, beliefs, or observations, it is not the declaration that i...

concepts.label: Declarative Power
concepts.description: A declarative power covers the case when an effect is produced through the party’s declaration of it

concepts.label: Decree
concepts.description: The word decree is often used as a derogative term for any authoritarian decision

concepts.label: Definitional Expression
concepts.description: A definition in a legal context (for example “x means y” or “by x it is meant y”);

concepts.label: Delegation
concepts.description: Delegate: entrust a task or responsibility to some other person

concepts.label: Delivery Date
concepts.description: The date when the competent authorities finalise the document by affixing their signatures to it (e.g. promulgation by the president, signature by the queen etc.) This is the date shown on the document itself: it is an objective element and clearly identifyable.

concepts.label: Deregulation
concepts.description: When a part of some primary legislative source is delegated to some secondary legislative source (e.g. from act to regulation).

concepts.label: Desire
concepts.description: A feeling of wanting

concepts.label: Directive
concepts.description: Examples are European Union directive, a legislative act of the European Union and Directives, used by United States Government agencies (particularly the Department of Defense) to convey policies, responsibilities, and procedures.

concepts.label: Disallowed
concepts.description: See Qualified. Alternative labels: violation, prohibited, forbidden

concepts.label: Disallowed Intention
concepts.description: The propositional content (i.e. that which is intended) of the intention is disallowed. Interesting concept for establishing mens rea (guilty mind), although 'disallowed' is a weaker qualification than criminal. Note the distinction between purposely committing a crime and knowingly committing a ...

concepts.label: Document
concepts.description: A Document bears some (and only) expression(s) stated by some statement in writing.

concepts.label: Dynamic Temporal Entity
concepts.description: A dynamic temporal entity represents the norm in its evolution over time.

concepts.label: Efficacy Interval
concepts.description: The period during which a normative fragment may be either operative or inoperative, by explicit provision of the document itself. The document is said to be in a period of operation, or enforceability or efficacy, when it may or must be applied or enforced.

concepts.label: Efficacy Modification
concepts.description: Modifies the efficacy period of some norm

concepts.label: Enabling Power
concepts.description: An enabling power is used in cases where the law aims at enabling some agent to produce an effect in a particular way.

concepts.label: End efficacy
concepts.description: Class

concepts.label: End in Force
concepts.description: When an act states the end of the period of enactment, and includes an implicit repealing of the text.

concepts.label: Enter in Force Date
concepts.description: The date when a dnormative document becomes law and enters the legal system for the first time. This is the moment in the doucment's history starting from which the document can be amended, its applicability assessed, and its manner of producing an effect determined.

concepts.label: Epistemic Role
concepts.description: The role of something used in a (mental) reasoning/inference process

concepts.label: Evaluative Attitude
concepts.description: An evaluative attitude expresses e.g. a judgment. The proposition qualified by the evaluative attitude is comparable to something else.

concepts.label: Evaluative Expression
concepts.description: A legal evaluative expression asserts that something is good or bad, is a value to be optimised or an evil to be minimised (for example “human dignity is value”, “participation ought to be promoted”);

concepts.label: Evaluative Proposition
concepts.description: Some thing which is evaluatively qualified, i.e. an evaluation applies to the proposition, the proposition is judged. The proposition is comparable to some other proposition.

concepts.label: Evidence
concepts.description: Observation and/or statement, used as a backing for a belief. Evidence is the role of observation which is qualified by some belief.

concepts.label: Exception
concepts.description: An exception is something that is excluded from a general statement or does not follow a rule. In LKIF rules, an exception is a rule which has an exception relation to another rule (cf. Deliverable 1.1)

concepts.label: Exclusionary Right
concepts.description: An exclusionary right concerns the prohibition against performing certain inferences (against reasoning in certain ways), or against using certain kinds of premises for certain purposes, in the interest of a particular person. This is especially the case with anti-discrimination rules.

concepts.label: Existence Date
concepts.description: The date when the formal act by which a legislative body freezes the document into its final form, it is the time when the document can be said to have begun its existence.

concepts.label: Existential Expression
concepts.description: Establishes or terminates the existence of a legal entity (for example “the company ceases to exist”);

concepts.label: Expectation
concepts.description: An expectation is a predictive belief held on purely logical grounds, i.e. not based on direct external evidence, like an observation or a statement by another agent. It is also often characterized as a "belief about the future", but this isn't very helpful since one may also hold expectations ab...

concepts.label: Expression
concepts.description: An expression is a proposition beared by some medium, e.g. a document, and is stated by some communicated attitude

concepts.label: Extension
concepts.description: Extends the scope of normative content to some particular jurisdiction

concepts.label: Fact
concepts.description: A fact is a proposition (about something) which is (commonly) agreed upon to hold as true: it has some backing in evidence

concepts.label: Foundation
concepts.description: A kind of (philanthropic) organization, set up as a legal entity either by individuals or institutions, with the purpose of distributing grants to support causes in line with the goals of the foundation

concepts.label: Function
concepts.description: The use or purpose of some object as used in some context.

concepts.label: Hohfeldian Power
concepts.description: A hohfeldian power covers any action which determines a legal effect.

concepts.label: Immunity
concepts.description: Also called Disabilities

concepts.label: In Force Interval
concepts.description: The period during which a normative fragment belongs to the normative system. The period of force for each fragment may change over time as a function of the modifications the document goes through.

concepts.label: In Force Modification
concepts.description: Modifies the period of being in force of some norm

concepts.label: Incorporated
concepts.description: An organisation formed into a legal corporation

concepts.label: Initiation
concepts.description: The initation of a change

concepts.label: Integration
concepts.description: Class

concepts.label: Intention
concepts.description: Intention is where the agent expects certain consequences of his or her actions and desires those consequences to occur. This concept must be related to qualification and preference in some way.

concepts.label: International Agreement
concepts.description: An agreement entered into by actors in international law, namely states and international organizations.

concepts.label: International Arbitration
concepts.description: International Arbitration is the established method today for resolving disputes between parties to international commercial agreements. As with arbitration generally, it is a creature of contract, i.e., the parties' decision to submit any disputes to private adjudication by one or more arbitrato...

concepts.label: Interpretation
concepts.description: Modification of the interpretation of normative content by the author or some superior actor

concepts.label: Interval
concepts.description: An interval is a composition of multiple periods of time.

concepts.label: Legal Doctrine
concepts.description: Legal doctrine is a framework, set of rules, procedural steps, or test, often established through precedent in the common law, through which judgments can be determined in a given legal cas

concepts.label: Legal Document
concepts.description: A legal document is a document bearing norms or normative statements. By virtue of this definition the norm-as-propositional-attitude is reified as norm-as proposition. In other words, the norm being expressed through the legal source is an expression of the propositional attitude.

concepts.label: Legal Expression
concepts.description: Legal expressions are created by  some legal speech act and qualified by a communicated attitude

concepts.label: Legal Person
concepts.description: A legal entity is a natural person or a legal construct through which the law allows a group of natural persons to act as if it were a single composite individual for certain purposes. The most common purposes are lawsuits, property ownership, and contracts. Sometimes referred to as corporate per...

concepts.label: Legal Role
concepts.description: A legal role is a role played in a legal context. Legal role players can be both Agents and other 'things'

concepts.label: Legal Source
concepts.description: A legal source is a source for legal statements, both norms and legal expressions. In a sense it is literally a 'source' of law

concepts.label: Legal Speech Act
concepts.description: A legal speech act creates some propositional attitude towards a legal expression.

concepts.label: Legislative Body
concepts.description: A legislature is a type of (representative) deliberative assembly with the power to adopt laws.

concepts.label: Liability Right
concepts.description: A liability right expresses some right to act that brings with it some liability to perform another (compensating) act. For instance, if some k performs the permitted action A, then k will have to perform another action B for the benefit of j.

concepts.label: Liberty Right
concepts.description: When, for the benefit of a person, this person is both permitted to perform and to omit an action – that is, when the action is facultative – we can say that he or she has a liberty right with regard to that action.

concepts.label: Lie
concepts.description: An assertion that is inconsistent with the beliefs of the speaker. It is *intentionally* false.

concepts.label: Limited Company
concepts.description: A limited company is a corporation whose liability is limited by law

concepts.label: Location Complex
concepts.description: A location complex is a relatively stable complex of places referred to as one: it is the maximal collection of places with the same reference object.

concepts.label: Mandate
concepts.description: Mandate: give (someone) authority to act in a certain way

concepts.label: Mandatory Precedent
concepts.description: In law, a binding precedent (also mandatory precedent or binding authority) is a precedent which must be followed by all lower courts. It is usually created by the decision of a higher court, such as the House of Lords in the United Kingdom. Binding precedent relies on the legal principle of star...

concepts.label: Medium
concepts.description: A medium is a bearer of expressions, i.e. externalised propositions. Propositions become expressions once they are externalised through some medium.

concepts.label: Mental Entity
concepts.description: We made the assumption that our views of the mental world have been developed in analogy with physical processes. Mental objects like thoughts are made of elementary parts: concepts. The contents (substance) of these objects are representations. The conceptual content of thoughts are intended by ...

concepts.label: Mental Object
concepts.description: Metaphor of physical concepts, i.e. the things we mentally manipulate, either in thought or memory

concepts.label: Mental Process
concepts.description: A mental, i.e. non-physical, process that has no physical effects. Examples are (human) thought and reasoning.

concepts.label: Modification
concepts.description: See ESTRELLA deliverable 3.2

concepts.label: Modification of Meaning
concepts.description: A modification that changes the meaning of some provision without changing its literal text

concepts.label: Modification of Scope
concepts.description: See ESTRELLA deliverable 3.2

concepts.label: Modification of System
concepts.description: See ESTRELLA deliverable 3.2

concepts.label: Modification of Term
concepts.description: Modification of the term specified by some procedural deadline.

concepts.label: Moment
concepts.description: A moment is an atomic period of time, i.e. it cannot be divided into other parts

concepts.label: Natural Object
concepts.description: A natural object is an object not created by man.

concepts.label: Natural Person
concepts.description: A natural person is a human being perceptible through the senses and subject to physical laws, as opposed to an artificial person, i.e., an organization that the law treats for some purposes as if it were a person distinct from its members or owner.

concepts.label: Negated Atom
concepts.description: A negated atom is the negation of some other atom (cf. Deliverable 1.1)

concepts.label: Non-binding International Agreement
concepts.description: Some international agreement that is not binding under international law

concepts.label: Norm
concepts.description: A norm is a kind of Qualification. A qualification which normatively qualifies some thing (i.e. some normatively qualified): i.e. a qualification which allows or disallows some thing.

concepts.label: Normatively Qualified
concepts.description: Some thing which is qualified (allowed, disallowed) by a norm, i.e. a norm applies to the thing. Taking the principle of deontic choice to mean that the utterer of a normative statement intends to influence choices made by the addressee of the statement, the qualified thing should is comparable t...

concepts.label: Obligation
concepts.description: See prohibition

concepts.label: Obligative Right
concepts.description: Directed obligative ought-to-do are also called obligative rights. k has the obligative  right that j does A iff it is obligatory, toward k, that j does A. An example of obligative  right is “it is obligatory, toward Mary, that Tom pays 1,000 euro to John”

concepts.label: Obliged
concepts.description: Is allowed by an Obligation, i.e. the alternative is strictly_worse according to the Obligation. Alternative labels: directed, commanded.

concepts.label: Observation
concepts.description: An observation is the role played by some proposition believed to be true or false through observation of an agent.

concepts.label: Observation of Violation
concepts.description: An observation of a violation, i.e. of something that is Disallowed.

concepts.label: Occurrence
concepts.description: A consequence of our clear separation of ontology from models of situations (occurrences), is well exemplified in the two ways we look at time and space. Things happen against the canvas of space and time. This 3D canvas moving in time (or whatever metaphor) allows us to index instances of object...

concepts.label: Organisation
concepts.description: An organisation is a group of other organisations or persons which acts 'as one'. An organisation can be both formal (i.e. created by law or decree) or informal.

concepts.label: Organisation Role
concepts.description: A role which has a meaning in the context of an organisation: i.e. the role defines a 'position' within sthe structure of roles within an organisation

concepts.label: Pair
concepts.description: A composition of exactly two parts

concepts.label: Pair Of Periods
concepts.description: A pair of two time periods

concepts.label: Part
concepts.description: A part is a part_of some whole

concepts.label: Permission
concepts.description: Permission allows propositions, to which therefore the predication Allowed applies. The thing(s) allowed is/are a subset of the thing(s) qualified by the permission. If S then P(A) means that S is qualified and S and A is allowed.

concepts.label: Permissive Right
concepts.description: The  negation of a directed obligation is a directed permission. However, it counts as a right,  namely, a permissive right, only when such negation is aimed at benefitting the author of  the permitted action.

concepts.label: Person
concepts.description: A person is an individual agent. Usually associated with 'human being'.

concepts.label: Person Role
concepts.description: A role played by some person (i.e. not an organisation)

concepts.label: Personal Plan
concepts.description: A personal plan is a plan which is held (and can be executed) by at most one agent.

concepts.label: Persuasive Precedent
concepts.description: In law, a persuasive precedent or advisory precedent is a precedent that need not be followed under the legal principle of stare decisis, but is nevertheless followed. Sources of persuasive precedent include the obiter dicta in the judgment of a court whose judgment would otherwise be binding, an...

concepts.label: Physical Entity
concepts.description: The physical world evolves around two main classes: physical objects and processes. In lkif-core, the physical world evolves around two main classes: physical objects and processes. Objects are pieces of matter, while matter is typed by substances. Objects have mass, extension, viz. form and aggr...

concepts.label: Physical Object
concepts.description: A physical object is a physical entity consisting of matter, it has a spatio-temporal extension.

concepts.label: Physical Process
concepts.description: Class

concepts.label: Place
concepts.description: A place is a spatio-temporal-occurrence

concepts.label: Plan
concepts.description: A plan is a structure of multiple other plans or actions. These can be both sequential or concurrent. Usually a plan is referred to in the context of the intention to act of some agent, however when executed the plan itself comes into effect.

concepts.label: Potestative Expression
concepts.description: Attributes a power to some agent (for example “a worker has the power to terminate his work contract”);

concepts.label: Potestative Right
concepts.description: A potestative right is an enabling power which is meant to benefit the holder of the power. For example, if some animal y does not belong to anybody, then x has the potestative-right to start x’s ownership of the animal,  by capturing y.

concepts.label: Precedent
concepts.description: In law, a precedent or authority is a legal case establishing a principle or rule that a court may need to adopt when deciding subsequent cases with similar issues or facts. The term may also refer to the collective body of case law that a court should consider when interpreting the law. When a p...

concepts.label: Legal Person (Private Law)
concepts.description: A legal person as defined in private law

concepts.label: Problem
concepts.description: A problem is an observation that deviates from an Intention.

concepts.label: Process
concepts.description: A process is a 'causal' change: any change which can be explained through some known or understood causal structure. Every process has some Time_Period as duration.

concepts.label: Proclamation
concepts.description: A proclamation (Lat. proclamare, to make public by announcement) is an official declaration.

concepts.label: Professional Legal Role
concepts.description: A professional legal role is a legal profession of some person, examples: lawyer, judge etc.

concepts.label: Prohibition
concepts.description: Prohibition obliges/allows thing(s), to which therefore the predication Obliged applies, and disallows thing(s), to which therefore the predication Disallowed applies. The union of the thing(s) allowed and the thing(s) disallowed is qualified by the prohibition. The things allowed and disallowed ...

concepts.label: Promise
concepts.description: A promise is a communicated attitude about some future action or state

concepts.label: Proposition
concepts.description: A (non logical) proposition is a proposition qualified by a propositional attitude. NB: The proposition used here does not correspond to a proposition in proposition logics.

concepts.label: Propositional Attitude
concepts.description: A propositional attitude connects a person (the holder of the attitude) to some proposition, in fact it expresses some qualification over the proposition. Distinguishing a proposition from the propositional content expressed by it is necessary when properties relating to the thing expressed and p...

concepts.label: Prorogation Efficacy
concepts.description: Prorogation of entry into force, but applied to the efficacy of some norm

concepts.label: Prorogation in Force
concepts.description: Prorogation of the date of enactment of some normative content. The 'life' of the act is lengthened with respect to some previous end of enactment modification.

concepts.label: Public Act
concepts.description: A public act is an act by some Person or Organisation which creates (at least) a communicated attitude (and thereby an expression)

concepts.label: Public Body
concepts.description: A public body or body created by an act of law to serve a public interest

concepts.label: PLC
concepts.description: Similar to the US corporation, offers several advantages over trading as sole trader.

concepts.label: Publication Date
concepts.description: The date when the normative document is published in the official journal designated as the source for making all such documents public and legal.

concepts.label: Qualification
concepts.description: A qualification expresses e.g. a judgment. The thing qualified by the qualification is comparable to something else.

concepts.label: Qualificatory Expression
concepts.description: Ascribes a legal role to a person or an object (for example,  “x is a citizen”, “x is an intellectual work”, “x is a technical invention”);

concepts.label: Qualified
concepts.description: Something that is qualified by some qualification

concepts.label: Ratification
concepts.description: When an international treaty is ratified by local parliament in order to include it in the local legal system. The same thing happens when each local parliament ratifies bilateral or multilateral agreements.

concepts.label: Reaction
concepts.description: A reaction is an action that is (at least) performed by an agent that has observed some other action (this is an intensional view): Action <-> Reaction

concepts.label: Reason
concepts.description: Teleological counterpart of cause

concepts.label: Regulation
concepts.description: A regulation bears one or more norms, all of which are uttered by some legislative body. It cannot bear expressions which are not uttered by a legislative body.

concepts.label: Relative Place
concepts.description: A relative place is defined by some reference to some object/thing

concepts.label: Relocation
concepts.description: Moving some part of the text to some other place within the same document

concepts.label: Remaking
concepts.description: When an act is completely rewritten in a new way but the topic remains the same.

concepts.label: Renewal
concepts.description: Class

concepts.label: Repeal
concepts.description: Removal of some part of text or the entire act from the legal system.

concepts.label: Resolution
concepts.description: A resolution is a written motion adopted by a deliberative body. The substance of the resolution can be anything that can normally be proposed as a motion.

concepts.label: Retroactivity
concepts.description: When the efficacy or a partial efficacy starts before the entry into force of the document

concepts.label: Right
concepts.description: A right is the legal or moral entitlement to do or refrain from doing something or to obtain or refrain from obtaining an action, thing or recogition in civil society.

concepts.label: Role
concepts.description: A role is a specification of default behavior and accompanying expectations of the thing 'playing' the role. Similar to actors in a theater who play roles, but are not the roles. Example: student.

concepts.label: Rule
concepts.description: An LKIF rule, based on swrl:Impl

concepts.label: Semantic Annotation
concepts.description: See ESTRELLA deliverable 3.2

concepts.label: Social Legal Role
concepts.description: A social legal role is played by some agent in the context of legal activities.

concepts.label: Social Role
concepts.description: A social role is played by some agent in the context of social activities. The social role brings with it some expectation of 'default' behavior of the role-filler.

concepts.label: Society
concepts.description: An organized group of people associated together for religious, benevolent, cultural, scientific, political, patriotic, or other purposes.

concepts.label: Soft Law
concepts.description: The term "soft law" refers to quasi-legal instruments which do not have any binding force, or whose binding force is somewhat "weaker" than the binding force of traditional law, often referred to as "hard law", in this context. The term "soft law" initially appeared in the area of international l...

concepts.label: Spatio Temporal Occurrence
concepts.description: An occurrence in space-time

concepts.label: Speech Act
concepts.description: A speech act (or illocutionary act) creates some propositional attitude which qualifies an expression (which by default is mediated through some medium). The actor of the speech act is the utterer of the atitude (NB cannot be expressed in OWL DL).

concepts.label: Start Efficacy
concepts.description: Class

concepts.label: Start in Force
concepts.description: Class

concepts.label: Statement In Writing
concepts.description: Not to be confused with the actual writing/document itself, which is the medium of the statement.

concepts.label: Static Temporal Entity
concepts.description: A static temporal entity captures a single moment in the norm's life that is fixed over time.

concepts.label: Statute
concepts.description: A statute bears one or more norms, all of which are uttered by some legal person. It cannot bear expressions which are uttered by a different kind of agent.

concepts.label: Strictly Allowed
concepts.description: Loose end.

concepts.label: Strictly Disallowed
concepts.description: Loose end.

concepts.label: Subjective Entity
concepts.description: A subjective entity is ontologically subjective, i.e. its existence is relative to an observer, that attributes its properties to some other entity, given a context.

concepts.label: Substitution
concepts.description: Substitution of a part or entire act or annex

concepts.label: Surprise
concepts.description: A surprise is an observation that deviates from an expectation.

concepts.label: Suspension
concepts.description: When a part of an act or some provisions are suspended in coming to be operative for a period or indefinately

concepts.label: Temporal Modification

concepts.label: Transaction
concepts.description: A transaction is an exchange or interaction between at least two agents a and b. Consists of two actions A and B where a is the actor of action A and the recipient of action B, and vice versa. Usually these actions are performed concurrently, but these may also be done consequently.
